S7 Base Class for Penalties

Source: R/penalty_class.R
penalty.Rd

This class is the abstract parent of every penalty in this package. A penalty is a scalar function of the coefficients, written \(\rho(D\beta; \theta)\): a linear map \(D\) that selects or combines coefficients, a scalar function \(\rho\) applied to what the map returns, and hyperparameters \(\theta\) that scale or shape it. The class holds no mathematics of its own. It records the pieces that every branch needs, so that a penalty's size, its hyperparameter names and their bounds can be read in the same way for every branch.

Usage

penalty(
  penalty_name = character(0),
  map = NULL,
  n_coef = integer(0),
  params = character(0),
  params_bounds = list(),
  link_params = list(),
  params_smooth = logical(0)
)

Arguments

penalty_name

A single string naming the penalty, used by print() and by any code that reports which penalty a block carries.

map

The matrix \(D\), of \(m\) rows and \(q\) columns, or NULL for the identity. A Matrix object is kept in its own storage, so a diagonal map, such as the map that standardization produces, is recognized as diagonal by its class.

n_coef

The number of coefficients \(q\). The value is a single whole number.

params

The hyperparameter names, in the order by which every derivative list is keyed. The value is character(0) for a penalty with none.

params_bounds

A named list with one entry per hyperparameter, and each entry is a numeric pair giving an open interval. A value at either endpoint is rejected, so (0, Inf) excludes zero.

link_params

A named list, one linkfunctions7 link per hyperparameter, carrying that hyperparameter's own interval onto the whole real line.

params_smooth

A logical vector, one entry per hyperparameter, TRUE where the value is differentiable in it.

Value

An S7 object of class penalty carrying the seven properties above. The class is abstract: an object of exactly this class can be printed, it receives the defaults listed under Methods, and penalty_value() and the other generics without a base method signal an error for it.

The properties

With \(q\) coefficients and a map of \(m\) rows, beta is a vector of length \(q\), \(D\beta\) has length \(m\), and every derivative in the coefficients is returned with length \(q\) or shape \(q \times q\). A NULL map is the identity, and then \(m = q\) and applying the map involves no arithmetic.

Each hyperparameter carries a linkfunctions7 link in link_params, which maps its own open interval onto the whole real line. A penalty can therefore be optimized on the unconstrained scale: a caller works in \(\eta = g(\theta)\), without bound constraints, and penalty_grad_theta(), penalty_hess_theta() and penalty_cross() return either scale through their scale argument.

params_smooth records in which hyperparameters the value is differentiable. It is TRUE for every hyperparameter of the quadratic, structured, additive, SCAD and MCP branches. A separable penalty copies the entries of its parent distribution, so a penalty built by distrib_penalty() on a Laplace distribution with a free location has FALSE for that location.

Writing a branch

This class is constructed directly only to write a new branch. A subclass supplies penalty_value(), penalty_gradient(), penalty_hessian(), penalty_grad_theta(), penalty_hess_theta(), penalty_cross(), penalty_kinks() and is_proper(), which have no method on the base class, and check_penalty() then compares the derivatives with numerical derivatives of the value. The methods registered on the base class, listed below, supply defaults for everything else.

The shipped branches are quadratic_penalty() (with ridge_penalty()), distrib_penalty() (with lasso_penalty() and elasticnet_penalty()), scad_penalty(), mcp_penalty(), additive_penalty() and structured_penalty(), which is built on a parameters7 matrix parameter.

Methods

The methods registered on penalty itself are inherited by every branch that does not register its own.

Predicates and readable quantities:

  • is_quadratic() returns FALSE.

  • penalty_readable() returns NULL.

  • beta_quadratic() returns FALSE.

Quantities of a quadratic penalty, which signal an error:

  • penalty_matrix(), penalty_rank(), penalty_null_basis() and penalty_logpdet().

Derivatives for a marginal criterion, which signal an error:

  • penalty_dhessian(), penalty_d2hessian() and penalty_dcross();

  • penalty_dhessian_beta();

  • penalty_d2hessian_beta() and penalty_dhessian_beta_theta().

Proximal operator:

  • penalty_prox() signals an error.

  • penalty_prox_spec() returns NULL.

Draws and printing:

  • penalty_draw() draws from a quadratic penalty read as a Gaussian prior and returns NA otherwise.

  • print() writes one line describing the penalty.

See also

quadratic_penalty(), distrib_penalty(), scad_penalty(), mcp_penalty(), additive_penalty() and structured_penalty() for the branches; penalty_value() and penalty_gradient() for what a branch supplies; check_penalty() to verify one.

Examples

# Every branch inherits from this class.
pen <- quadratic_penalty(crossprod(diff(diag(4))), map = NULL)
S7::S7_inherits(pen, penalty)
#> [1] TRUE

# These properties can be read in the same way for every branch.
pen@penalty_name
#> [1] "quadratic"
pen@n_coef
#> [1] 4
pen@params
#> [1] "lambda"
pen@params_bounds
#> $lambda
#> [1]   0 Inf
#> 

# A first-difference map over three coefficients takes three coefficients
# in and returns two rows.
D <- diff(diag(3))
mapped <- quadratic_penalty(diag(2), map = D)
mapped
#> quadratic penalty on 3 coefficient(s) through 2 row(s); theta: lambda
